question: Which native change and identity contracts should providers reuse for local, remote and reconnect behavior?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; Task final-plan adversarial review; Redesign from First Principles; Benchmark performance-review lens; three bounded independent source/caller/proof challenges
trigger: After the collaboration design plan was presented as ready, the user asked to make sure nothing was forgotten and requested harsh honest feedback. Scope is planning and review repair only; no product implementation or publication.
requirements: Reject waiting/error document and shared-effect work before publication and history; compensation after an invalid commit is insufficient.
Surface shared-effect decode/import failure as stable admission error, retain unacknowledged work, and recover exactly once through retry.
Preserve one controller and compaction authority per Y.Doc namespace while allowing same-factory presentation extension and multiple mounted views.
Keep provider resources and provider-specific readiness adapters app-owned; a seed grant requires an exclusive external room-creation decision.
Remove live collaboration state from replayable read.yjs and infer presence/compaction API methods only when their capabilities are configured.
Preserve the independent public YjsUpdatePolicy custom-adapter job and specify exact Plite/Plate headless and React exports.
Prove the combined lifecycle/API target with balanced A/A and A/B measurements, real-provider/browser behavior, TypeScript 7 inference and packed declarations before implementation-ready status.
evidenceReuse: Reused current-source initial review, API/admission probes and benchmark receipts only within their recorded limits. Rechecked live Yjs controller, shared-effect log, Plate facade, package barrels, Hocuspocus and registry consumers, public Plite docs, generated/export tooling and benchmark harness. Three independent read-only challenges covered state/lifetime failure modes, public callers/exports and measurement validity. A disposable source-backed claimed-empty probe observed convergent concurrent block insertions. No product source was changed.
summary: Defer product implementation. The ownership cuts remain directionally sound, especially deleting transport commands, the duplicate Plate store and live read.yjs, but the plan was falsely labeled ready. It lacked a composite candidate; swallowed shared-effect failures, invalid waiting/error commit compensation, compaction replacement conflict, post-publication failure semantics and multi-view awareness arbitration remain unresolved. The review also cuts the unearned public Hocuspocus helper, retains YjsUpdatePolicy, makes API capabilities conditional, selects concrete demo seed ownership, adds an exact export/adoption matrix and rejects the order-confounded benchmark as acceptance.
alternatives: Execute the former plan unchanged: reject; separate API/admission prototypes and an order-confounded benchmark cannot support implementation-ready status.
Keep current APIs and patch local defects: reject as the durable target because transport commands, duplicate Plate configuration and live ambient state remain under the wrong lifetimes.

Export a neutral Hocuspocus readiness helper: cut; one real app caller already owns the adapter and this checkout installs materially different Hocuspocus versions without package-level compatibility proof.
Privatize YjsUpdatePolicy with diagnostics: reject; current public Plite docs use it for an independent host-owned canonical-change adapter job.

Expose all API methods and throw when capabilities are missing: reject for typed callers; infer presence and compaction methods only when awareness or compaction authority is supplied, with erased-boundary guards.
Grant seed:true to every demo peer after sync: reject; choose one externally exclusive room-generation owner, using unique ephemeral Hocus rooms or a single in-memory DemoRoom owner.
Pursue one composite native candidate under the corrected ownership and export target: selected investigation; it can settle lifecycle feasibility and performance before product adoption.
proofLimits: No product implementation, TypeScript 7 packed declaration proof, real Hocuspocus server run, mounted browser proof or combined lifecycle/API candidate exists. Current shared-effect errors are swallowed, waiting/error writes use commit-plus-compensation, same-document replacement can conflict with compaction authority and post-publication observer failure cannot restore the old binding. The calibrated benchmark reports 15 passes but gives baseline the cold-first construction position twice, compares independent medians, misses a direct normal construction pair and measures only cursor-data API relocation. Claimed-empty required-minimum behavior was observed only in a disposable native probe. The corrected plan intentionally remains incomplete.
